title: Atmosphere dome e2e pixel probe (density scaling in rendered pixels) + TASK-28 close-out
description: The one TASK-28 acceptance criterion not yet literally met: 'Haze density scales with planet.atmosphereDensity (a thin-atmosphere planet is visibly less hazy — two planets in the seeded galaxy differ, asserted in a render test: haze factor at mid-boundary differs by > 20%)'. The PURE-MATH counterpart is already committed (src/shared/galaxy/planets.test.ts asserts a seeded pair differs by > 20%). This task renders the atmosphere dome at mid-boundary for a minimum-haze and a maximum-haze atmospheric planet through a REAL WebGL renderer in the headless Playwright harness, samples the center pixel, and asserts the density scaling is visible in the rendered colors AND that the rendered color matches the shared-math mix. Then it runs the full verification and does the TASK-28 close-out — this is the LAST split task, so it is the one that marks TASK-28 done, writes the LOG entry, and deletes the handoff.

steps.description: Dev-only pixel-probe hook — NEW src/client/atmosphere-debug.ts (~150 lines)
steps.details: Pattern: src/client/camera/camera-debug.ts (dev-only `window.__ATMO__` hook, gated on `import.meta.env.DEV`, no-op in prod). Expose `midBoundaryComparison()`: (a) read the seed from `window.__DRIFT__.seed` (fed from /api/health at module load, no login needed — fail loudly if missing, same as camera-debug's hook.seed check). (b) Scan `generateStars(seed)` (cap the scan at ~40 systems for speed) via `generateSystem(seed, star.id)`; collect atmospheric planets (hasAtmosphere) with `hazeMid = hazeFactor(ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY_M / 2, { atmosphereRadius: planetAtmosphereRadius(p), atmosphereDensity: planetAtmosphereDensity(p) })`; take the min-hazeMid and max-hazeMid pair (the spec AC is a relative diff > 0.2 — fail loudly if the seed yields no such pair). (c) For EACH of the two planets, in isolation: an offscreen `document.createElement('canvas')` 128x72, `new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas, antialias: false, preserveDrawingBuffer: true })`, `renderer.setSize(128, 72, false)`, a fresh `THREE.Scene()` with `scene.background = new THREE.Color('#0d1626')` (this is the CLEAR color the expected pixel lerps from); `dome = createAtmosphereDome(planetAtmosphereRadius(p))` positioned at `planetAnchor(index)` where index is the planet's orbital-slot index within ITS system's planets; camera at anchor + (0, 500, 0) looking horizontal (`camera.lookAt(anchor.x, 500, anchor.z + 100)`), far 5000; `dome.set(hazeMid, <any> )`. THEN — CRITICAL — override the dome uniforms with RAW sRGB floats so the raw ShaderMaterial output is free of color-space transforms and the expected pixel is EXACT: `(dome.material.uniforms.uAtmoColor.value as THREE.Vector3).set(r/255, g/255, b/255)` where r,g,b come from parsing ATMOSPHERE_HAZE_COLORS[p.class], and set `uSkyColor` the same way from the clear color '#0d1626'. `renderer.render(scene, camera)`; `renderer.getContext().readPixels(centerX, centerY, 1, 1, RGBA, UNSIGNED_BYTE, buf)` the center pixel; then `renderer.dispose()` + `dome.dispose()` (no WebGL context leak). (d) Return `{ seed, a: { systemId, planetId, planetClass, density, hazeMid, pixel: [r,g,b], expected: [r,g,b] }, b: { ... }, hazeDiff, pixelError }` where `expected[ch] = lerp(clearF[ch], atmoF[ch], hazeMid) * 255` and `pixelError = max over channels of |pixel - expected|` (report the per-planet max; the spec asserts ≤ 3 on the worse of the two).

Add `installAtmosphereDebug();` next to the other dev-only installers at the bottom of main.tsx (after `installCameraDebug();`, line ~570) with a short comment (e.g. `// TASK-28.3: dev-only atmosphere dome pixel-probe hook (no-op in prod).`). Import installAtmosphereDebug from '@client/atmosphere-debug'. No behavior change beyond registering window.__ATMO__ in DEV.

Pattern: tests/e2e/streaming-budget.spec.ts (imports `expect, test` from './fixtures', `collectErrors` from './helpers'). `test.setTimeout(60_000);` (cold vite transform of the app + three.js). In the test: `const { assertClean } = collectErrors(page);`; `await page.goto(e2eServer.baseURL);`; poll `await expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => window.__DRIFT__?.seed ?? null), { timeout: 15_000, message: '__DRIFT__ server seed never arrived' }).not.toBeNull();`; `const result = await page.evaluate(() => window.__ATMO__!.midBoundaryComparison());`; `console.log` the recorded values (a/b planetClass + density + hazeMid + pixel + expected, like TASK-26.2's console.log) so they land in the test output; assert `result.hazeDiff > 0.2` (the density AC), `result.pixelError <= 3` (rendered dome color matches the shared-math mix — the density scaling is visibly in the pixels), and that the two sampled pixels visibly differ (max per-channel |a.pixel - b.pixel| > 5); `await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(__dirname, '../../../.ralph/screenshots/TASK-28.3-1.png') });`; `assertClean();`; close the context. No login needed (hook installs at module load; the seed arrives unauthenticated from /api/health). Mirror any constants (ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY_M=1000) locally if imported — the Playwright runner does not resolve the app's tsconfig path aliases.

steps.description: Full verification + TASK-28 close-out (LAST split task)
steps.details: Run in order from app/: `npx vitest run` (full unit suite green, ~85 s), `npm run typecheck` (clean), `npm run lint` (eslint + prettier --write on touched files if needed), then `npx playwright test --config playwright.e2e.config.ts atmosphere` (the e2e fixtures boot the real app themselves — do NOT start `npm run dev` manually; run the new spec TWICE, headless WebGL can be flaky on first GPU init). Playwright smoke of the running app (console clean) + a screenshot per AGENTS.md into .ralph/screenshots/TASK-28.3-{n}.png. Bookkeeping: `.ralph/tasks.json` — set passes: true for TASK-28.1, TASK-28.2, TASK-28.3 (and the parent TASK-28 entry, however Ralph's split registered it — match how TASK-25/26 split tasks were recorded); set the 4 step `pass` flags to true in `.ralph/tasks/TASK-28.json` (check how recent tasks recorded step passes in `.ralph/logs/LOG.md`); newest-first entry in `.ralph/logs/LOG.md` with the measured haze/pixel numbers + screenshot paths; update `.ralph/STRUCTURE.md` only if directories changed (none expected — all new files live in existing dirs: src/client/world, src/client/state, src/client/ui, src/client, tests/e2e). DELETE `.ralph/handoff/TASK-28.md` in the final commit. Kill any background processes, make ONE Conventional Commit (e.g. `test(TASK-28.3): atmosphere dome e2e pixel probe (density scaling in rendered pixels) + TASK-28 close-out`), output `<promise>TASK-28.3:DONE</promise>`, and STOP.

acceptanceCriteria: An e2e test renders the atmosphere dome at mid-boundary for a min-haze and a max-haze atmospheric planet (real WebGL renderer, headless Playwright) and asserts the haze/density difference > 20% (hazeDiff > 0.2) — the 'per-planet density in a render test' AC

The rendered dome center pixel matches the shared-math mix lerp(sky, atmo, hazeMid) within 3/255 per channel (pixelError ≤ 3), and the two planets' sampled pixels visibly differ (max per-channel diff > 5)
The __ATMO__ hook is dev-only (import.meta.env.DEV gate), never ships in a production build; every WebGLRenderer / dome / geometry is disposed so no WebGL context leaks
cd app && npx vitest run green, cd app && npm run typecheck clean, cd app && npm run lint clean, and cd app && npx playwright test --config playwright.e2e.config.ts atmosphere green twice in a row

TASK-28 close-out complete: tasks.json passes flags set for all split tasks (and the parent), TASK-28 spec step passes set, LOG.md newest-first entry with measured numbers + screenshot paths, .ralph/handoff/TASK-28.md deleted, committed and the working tree is clean
notes: DEPENDS ON TASK-28.1 AND TASK-28.2 (commit both first). The probe itself is STANDALONE (it renders createAtmosphereDome directly, not the live WorldManager), so it could technically build on 44202f3 alone — but this task is LAST because it does the TASK-28 close-out (full-suite green over the COMPLETE client, bookkeeping, delete the handoff). Do NOT close out until 28.1 + 28.2 are committed and green.

WHY E2E: three.js WebGLRenderer needs a real GL context; the vitest env (node/happy-dom) has none. The Playwright harness already runs headless WebGL successfully (core-flow.spec.ts, camera-handoff.spec.ts, streaming-budget.spec.ts) — this is the established path; the hook pattern (camera-debug.ts) and the spec pattern (streaming-budget.spec.ts) already exist.

ALREADY COMMITTED (44202f3) and reused here: createAtmosphereDome + ATMOSPHERE_HAZE_COLORS + DOME_SKY_COLOR (src/client/render/atmosphere-dome.ts); hazeFactor + ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY_M (src/shared/physics/atmosphere.ts); planetAtmosphereDensity + planetAtmosphereRadius + planetAnchor (src/shared/galaxy/planets.ts); generateStars (src/shared/galaxy/stars.ts — default GALAXY_STAR_COUNT=200, pass a count to bound the scan); generateSystem (src/shared/galaxy/system.ts); and the pure-math > 20% density-diff assertion (src/shared/galaxy/planets.test.ts — this task is its RENDER counterpart; the hook can reuse the same planet-selection idea).

DEAD END — three.js ColorManagement (the #1 risk for the pixel math): `new THREE.Color(hex)` converts sRGB→linear working space, but the dome's raw ShaderMaterial writes gl_FragColor with NO output transform → it renders too dark and the expected-pixel math breaks. ALWAYS feed raw 0..1 sRGB floats: in the probe, override the dome's uAtmoColor/uSkyColor uniform Vector3s DIRECTLY with r/255, g/255, b/255 parsed from ATMOSPHERE_HAZE_COLORS[p.class] / the clear color, so expected[ch] = lerp(clearF, atmoF, hazeMid) * 255 is exact. Keep preserveDrawingBuffer: true on the probe renderer (readPixels outside the rAF loop, headless SwiftShader).

BUDGET (45-min iteration): e2e boot is ~40 s per test file (worker-scoped, boots the app once per file). Put ALL assertions in the single atmosphere.spec.ts so the harness boots once. Do NOT run the full 8-file e2e suite — the gate is the new spec + the unit suite + typecheck + lint. If the min/max pair discovery or the pixel tolerance proves flaky, the pure-math fallback is already committed in planets.test.ts; prefer tightening the probe (raw-sRGB uniform override, a fixed camera that reliably sees the dome band) over relaxing the > 20% / pixelError ≤ 3 asserts.

Screenshot dir .ralph/screenshots/ already exists (TASK-27-1/2.png, TASK-26.2-1.png are there). The e2e screenshot path uses a relative path from tests/e2e (path.join(__dirname, '../../../.ralph/screenshots/TASK-28.3-1.png')) exactly like streaming-budget.spec.ts.
